reader.notes: The integer screen (IntegerViolation + NotAlwaysIntegral) refuses fraction literals, scaled items, a bare numeric function, quotients, scaled sums and fractional powers, but a numeric function that is one TERM of a sum or product clears AdditiveSpine.RestIntegral and the screen fails open (the code comment at NotAlwaysIntegral says so). FUNCTION SQRT(N) + 64 is the same value as N ** 0.5 + 64, which the PB5208 power arm refuses, so the gap is a missing witness arm for a numeric-function term (e.g. SQRT/LOG/trig of a bare item), not an undecidable shape. The screen is by design sound-not-complete (PB617, PB1526); this verdict is PARTIAL on that one shape.
